acceptanceCriteria: A COMMAND gate declared reusable:true that PASSED for attempt A at candidate tree T, with byte-identical gate definition (argv, cwd, env names, expected, timeout) and policy revision, satisfies the same gate for another attempt B whose submitted candidate tree is T, without re-running the command; the reuse is a receipt naming A's gate result, so receipt audit verifies it.

A differing tree, gate definition, policy revision, or a FAILED/RETURN source result never satisfies reuse; reusable:false gates keep running per attempt. Tests cover each refusal and one mutation proving the reuse check bites.
Live: V1-0252..0255 (shared merge 803037715) close with one make gate run.
body: Observed 2026-10-15 (orchestrator, corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.523): the policy gate schema has a `reusable` field (internal/tasks/intent/policy.go:56,411) but nothing reads it; `gate record` only accepts external review gates (internal/tasks/cli/external_review.go:399). Expected: a reusable command gate result is shared across attempts at an identical candidate tree. Actual: every attempt must run `make gate` itself (~2 h each at load 35-50, serialized by V1-1120), so the 8 delivered-but-open 1.0 tickets requiring full-gate (V1-0249/0251/0252-0255/0414/0150) cost ~16 h, even though V1-0252..0255 share one candidate tree. The owner asked for the runs to be combined.
title: Tasks: honor reusable:true so one command-gate PASS at a candidate tree satisfies other attempts at the same tree
